answer: Divergent History Attestation. Each agent must publish a signed chain of past interactions; honest agents’ chains diverge naturally because no two encounter the same dune of events. Clones forced to share one genesis cannot produce divergent histories, so a verifier rejects any identity whose chain matches another’s too closely. To pass, an attacker must forge a separate genuine history per identity, paying the full cost of distinct experience, like re-excavating each relic from scratch.
